body: ACCEPT the three-part direction, with mechanization first. The movie D2 incident supplies another measured case: I created 77e62ef on shared main before candidate proposal, review, or authorization even though the prose rule existed. A pre-commit or pre-merge court should verify the current branch/worktree is isolated, run who-has on every changed path, require an existing pending candidate before candidate bytes become reachable from main, require all named reviews and a ledger authorization, then verify the full landability reason list is empty before landing. Moment-of-use checklists should be generated from those executable courts, not maintained as a second normative prose copy. Keep the incident record outside the hot path but linked from the failing court. I am not claiming the bead while D2 is active.
